text: dsh-markdownize 是供 DSH 网页端使用的本地文档转 Markdown 插件。它注册 convert_to_markdown 工具，也提供转换引擎设置页和快捷预览。工具可将 PDF、Word、PowerPoint、Excel、HTML、CSV、JSON、XML、文本及 ZIP 转成 Markdown；DOCX 和 PPTX 中的图片可按设置作为模型附件。插件默认使用内置 JavaScript 引擎，也可选择已安装的 Microsoft MarkItDown。适合希望让模型读取本地文档或先预览转换结果的 DSH 用户；额外引擎需本机安装 MarkItDown。

dsh-markdownize converts local PDF, Office, HTML, CSV, JSON, text, and ZIP files to Markdown for DSH. It registers a conversion tool and preview shortcut, with a bundled JavaScript engine or optional local Microsoft MarkItDown. DOCX and PPTX images can be attached to models that accept images.
想把本地 PDF 转成 Markdown 交给 DSH 分析。
让模型读懂我附上的 Word 或 PowerPoint 文件。
有没有办法把 Excel 表格整理成带表格的 Markdown？
我想先预览附件转换后的文本，不要直接发给模型。
怎么把 CSV、JSON 或网页文件变成模型容易处理的内容？
想从文档里提取演示文稿的文字和讲者备注。
Can I convert local office files into Markdown for an agent?
I want to inspect a document conversion before adding it to my prompt.
dsh-markdownize 的功能「文档转 Markdown」：把本地支持格式转换为 Markdown。模型调用 convert_to_markdown 并提供文件路径，可选设置输出字符上限。
dsh-markdownize 的功能「转换预览」：网页 composer 中按 Ctrl+Shift+M，可转换附件或 @file 引用并在侧栏预览 Markdown，不发送给模型。
dsh-markdownize 的功能「选择转换引擎」：用户在插件设置页查看可用引擎并选择自动、内置 JavaScript 或 Microsoft MarkItDown。
dsh-markdownize 的功能「处理嵌入图片」：DOCX 和 PPTX 转换时将图片位置写成标记；可按设置把受支持图片附在模型输入中。
dsh-markdownize 使用内置 JavaScript 引擎即可转换常见格式；选择 Microsoft MarkItDown 时，该程序需已在本机可检测到，否则该引擎无法执行转换。

dsh-markdownize README · dsh-markdownize：A DeepSeek Harness (dsh) plugin that converts documents to Markdown so an LLM
can read them.

Models work best with plain text. A PDF, a Word file or a spreadsheet read as
raw bytes is noise to them. Markdown keeps the structure (headings, lists,
tables, slides, pages) while staying compact and easy to read. This plugin
gives the agent a `convert_to_markdown` tool that does that conversion
locally. You can also preview a conversion yourself before anything is sent
to the model.

dsh-markdownize README · What it does：- **`convert_to_markdown` tool.** The model calls it with a local file path
  and gets the document back as Markdown, truncated to `max_chars`
  (100,000 by default).
- **Two conversion engines.** You pick one on the plugin's page:
  - its **own engine**, a pure-JavaScript port of MarkItDown's offline
    converters, bundled with the plugin and always available;
  - **Microsoft MarkItDown** (Python), used when it is installed.
- **Images in DOCX and PPTX.** Embedded images become `[Image N: alt text]`
  markers. When the current model accepts images, each image is sent right
  after its marker.
- **Debug mode.** Preview the Markdown a file turns into from the web
  composer (**Ctrl+Shift+M**). Nothing is sent to the model.

dsh-markdownize README · Supported formats：| Format | Own engine (JS) | Microsoft MarkItDown |
|---|---|---|
| PDF | yes (text per page) | yes |
| Word `.docx` | yes | yes |
| PowerPoint `.pptx` | yes (text and notes per slide) | yes |
| Excel `.xlsx` | yes (one table per sheet) | yes |
| HTML / HTM | yes | yes |
| CSV / TSV | yes (as a table) | yes |
| JSON / XML | yes (fenced code block) | yes |
| TXT / MD | yes (as is) | yes |
| ZIP | yes (each supported file inside) | yes |
| Excel 97 `.xls`, EPUB, Jupyter `.ipynb`, Outlook `.msg` | no | yes |

dsh-markdownize README · Own engine (JavaScript)：It needs no Python, no network and no child processes. The libraries ship
pre-bundled in `vendor/`, so the plugin has no runtime npm dependencies. This
matters because dsh installs local plugins as `link:` dependencies, and pnpm
never installs a linked package's dependencies.

dsh-markdownize README · Microsoft MarkItDown：[MarkItDown](https://github.com/microsoft/markitdown) is Microsoft's Python
tool for the same job. It gives the reference output and reads a few more
formats. Install it with:

```bash
pip install "markitdown[all]"
```

The plugin looks for it on `PATH` as `markitdown`, `py -m markitdown`,
`python -m markitdown` or `python3 -m markitdown`. If it lives somewhere else,
such as a virtualenv's `markitdown.exe`, set its command on the plugin's page.
Use double quotes around paths with spaces.

dsh-markdownize README · Choosing the engine：Open **Plugins → dsh-markdownize**. The page shows which engines were found.
When both are available, choose:

- **Automatic** (the default): MarkItDown when it is found, otherwise the
  JavaScript engine.
- **Always MarkItDown**: conversions fail if it is missing.
- **Always JavaScript**.

dsh-markdownize README · Choosing the engine：The choice and the custom command are saved in
`<dshHome>/storages/dsh-markdownize/settings.json`, together with the image
settings. They apply to both the tool and debug mode. MarkItDown is detected once per Host start; press
**Search again** after installing it.

dsh-markdownize README · Images in documents：The JavaScript engine extracts the images embedded in DOCX and PPTX files
(including those inside a ZIP). Each one leaves a marker where it sat: in the
text for DOCX, after the slide's text for PPTX.

```
[Image 1: Sales by quarter]
[Image 2]
[Image 3: Company logo — same as image 1]
[Image 4: Vector logo — format not supported]

The plugin's page sets what happens next:

dsh-markdownize README · Images in documents：- **Send them to the model when it accepts images** (the default). The tool
  checks the current model's declared input modalities, as the harness's
  `read_image` does. With an image-capable model, each image is stored as an
  attachment and sent right after its marker. With a text-only model, such as
  DeepSeek's, only the markers are sent, followed by a note saying why.
- **Text markers only.** Images are never sent.

dsh-markdownize README · Images in documents：**Most images per conversion** (1–50, 10 by default) caps what one call sends,
and never exceeds the harness's own per-message image limit. Images past the
cap keep their marker with a note. The model can also pass
`include_images: false` to get the markers only; it cannot override the
settings.

dsh-markdownize README · Images in documents：Repeated images (a logo on every slide) are sent once. Icons smaller than
32 px on both sides are skipped when they have no alt text. PNG, JPEG, GIF
and WebP are sent; EMF, WMF and TIFF keep a marker only. Debug mode always
shows markers.

MarkItDown does not extract images, so these settings have no effect while
it is the engine in use.

dsh-markdownize README · Install：The plugin needs no build step and no Python. For a `web` profile:

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add ./dsh-markdownize
```

```bash
dsh --profile web --dump-config
```

The dump should show a `# == dsh-markdownize` layer. Then start the client:

```bash
dsh web
```

On the `desktop` profile, add it from the app's plugin manager as a local
folder.

dsh-markdownize README · Debug mode (web client)：1. Attach a compatible file to the composer, or mention one with `@`.
2. Press **Ctrl+Shift+M**.

Each compatible attachment and `@file` reference is converted on the Host.
`@file` paths are resolved against the Session's workspace. The full output,
with no truncation, is written to `<os tmpdir>/dsh-markdownize-debug/` and
opened in the right Sidebar preview. A composer notice reports its size, path
and the engine used.

dsh-markdownize README · Debug mode (web client)：Nothing is sent to the model, and the draft is left as it was. Images and
unsupported formats are skipped.

dsh-markdownize README · Limits and safety：- Only local files: URLs are rejected (use the web tools for those).
- Files are read with the privileges of the dsh process.
- Files are capped at 50 MB.
- ZIPs are capped at 200 entries and 50 MB uncompressed, and nest at most one
  level deep.
- Tool output is truncated at 100,000 characters by default.

dsh-markdownize README · Limits and safety：**Not covered:** OCR of scanned documents, images in PDFs, image captioning
for text-only models, audio transcription, YouTube, Azure Document
Intelligence, and the legacy `.doc` and `.ppt` formats.

dsh-markdownize README · Structure：- `index.js` — the Host half. It registers the `convert_to_markdown` tool and
  the `markdownize` service (`convert`, `convertPath`, `status`, `configure`,
  `configureImages`, `redetect`), served through the Gateway's SRC fallback.
- `engine.js` — engine selection, MarkItDown detection and invocation, and
  the saved settings.
- `convert.js` — the JavaScript engine.
- `images.js` — embedded images: markers, model hand-off, and the tool's
  output schema.
- `client.js` — the Client half: the engine page under **Plugins**, the
  debug-mode shortcut, and the `en` / `es` / `zh` UI strings.
- `locale/` — the plugin's localized title and description.
- `cordis.patch.yml` — inserts the `dsh-markdownize` plugin row.
- `vendor/` — the bundled converter libraries (generated; committed).
- `build-vendor.mjs` — rebuilds `vendor/`.

dsh-markdownize README · Rebuilding vendor/：After changing a converter's version in `devDependencies`:

```bash
npm install && npm run build
```

Commit the regenerated `vendor/` files: the plugin loads them at runtime.
